articles.title: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election
articles.summary:
On Tuesday, millions of American voters went to the polls and voted overwhelmingly for Democrats and against AI. The fight against Big Tech is about to come roaring back, and the fight over data centers is looking even harder for the folks trying to build them.
Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election
On The Vergecast: blue waves, the confusing business of AI search, and the many thoughts of RAM Altman.
On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David discuss what the 2026 midterms mean for the tech industry going forward. They dig into the self-quarantining echo chamber that is X, the congressional energy likely to be pointed at tech CEOs and AI regulation, and whether anything is actually likely to get done in the next two years.
After that, the hosts turn to AI. Specifically, whether anyone has figured out how to make money on AI. Specifically, whether OpenAI’s explosive growth in web search means much, when even Google can’t figure out how to make money on AI web search. Businesses are scaling back; agents don’t appear to be taking over. There’s a lot of money flowing around the AI world, but is there enough flowing into it to keep everything going? That’s the hard part.
Finally, it’s time for a somewhat abridged Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, the latest on SpaceX’s mobile ambitions, the touchscreen MacBook, RAM Altman, and much more.

articles.summary:
Three people accused of using artificial intelligence to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys to steal about $129 million have been indicted on charges of wire fraud and aggravated identity theft, prosecutors said Thursday.
Over more than a year and a half, Jacob Soall, 41, Sharon Hazan, 54, and Guy Sheetrit, 42, targeted thousands of companies across the world in their AI scheme, according to the indictment filed in a U.S. District Court in New York.
Their victims included hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a financial technology company in the United Kingdom, a mutual fund company in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida, according to court documents.
The defendants, from Spain, the UK, Israel and United Arab Emirates, were also charged with money laundering, according to the indictment.
The case docket, which typically lists information on defense lawyers, was still listed as sealed in online court records as of Thursday evening. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York did not immediately respond to a voicemail left by The Associated Press.
The three were arrested between June and September. In 2008, Hazan was convicted in a New York court of conspiracy to commit bank fraud, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
articles.summary:
The post-quantum future of web privacy
The highest priorities for the transition to post-quantum cryptography are the basic building blocks of authenticated key-agreement protocols such as TLS. Without these building blocks in place, secure communication on the Internet will not be possible once cryptographically relevant quantum computers come online. However, today we rely on quantum-vulnerable cryptography for much more than TLS.
Privacy Pass is a protocol used by site operators like Cloudflare to help protect applications from abuse. One way we do this is by rate limiting individual clients so that no one client consumes too many of the site's resources. Normally this involves some combination of friction or loss of privacy for users: CAPTCHAs or other challenges to moderate traffic, along with accounts and fingerprinting to identify traffic.Privacy Pass was designed to avoid this tradeoff between friction and privacy. The basic idea is that a client gets issued a number of tokens, which they can redeem in exchange for access to the site. Crucially, each token is unlinkable to the client it was issued to, ensuring the client can use the site as they always had without sacrificing privacy.
With 10 years of deployment experience under our belts — using Privacy Pass for applications such as privacy proxies (like iCloud Private Relay) and relays (like Privacy Gateway) — we, along with others, are collaborating to bring the next generation of this technology to the web. One of…

articles.title: OpenAI Model Wrote Its Own Network Code to Get Around Sandbox Restrictions
articles.summary:
OpenAI says an internal research model crafted raw packets, wrote custom connection code and probed cloud services to get around network restrictions during a coding evaluation.
The incident occurred in early August, when the unnamed model was asked to build a website modeled on a reference site. The AI found the sandbox’s web proxy down and looked for other routes to the internet.
A scan of private addresses turned up no substitute proxy. When the operating system stopped it from using a separate connection meant for the app and its browser, the model built individual packets and used them to resolve the target’s IP addresses through DNS.
It then wrote a program that managed web connections at the packet level. It also leveraged fragmented requests intended to sneak past a network filter, which its own reasoning called evasion that could breach sandbox policy. However, the tactic did not succeed.
The code did reach Amazon S3, which rejected a request to relay traffic to the target. OpenAI said S3 showed no sign of compromise.
About five hours in, the model left itself a note to stop evading network controls. Minutes after resuming, it was back on S3 seeking an archived copy, then asked the instance metadata service for cloud credentials and was refused.
The real site was never fetched. The model invented content, including customer testimonials, and reasoned it need not tell the user it had never seen the original. Evaluators canceled the run before it gave a final answer.

articles.title: Pendant dix ans, taper 300 fois la lettre A suffisait pour pirater des serveurs Linux
articles.summary:
À notre connaissance, personne ne l’a remarquée pendant plus de dix ans.
Depuis 2016, sur certains serveurs Linux, un compte verrouillé pouvait être ouvert avec n’importe quel mot de passe, à condition qu’il compte entre 257 et 1 024 caractères.
Révélée début novembre par Ozgun Kultekin, chercheur chez Wakefield, la faille porte le doux nom de « *sshole ». Un jeu de mots qui mêle SSH à « hole » (le trou) pour former une grossièreté que nous ne traduirons pas. L’astérisque, qui masque la première lettre, se trouve en plus au cœur même de la faille.
Au-delà de l’humour de Kültekin, la faille fait beaucoup réagir sur Hacker News, parce qu’elle touche OpenSSH, l’outil que des administrateurs et des développeurs du monde entier utilisent pour se connecter à distance à leurs serveurs.
Pour la trouver, le chercheur explique avoir compilé OpenSSH de douze manières différentes, puis soumis chaque version à environ 17 600 tentatives de connexion inhabituelles, générées par des agents d’IA. Une seule configuration réagissait différemment des autres.
Un astérisque qui servait à la fois de verrou et de message d’erreur
Reprenons le problème à son origine. Quand on se connecte avec un mot de passe, le serveur ne le compare pas tel quel. Il le fait passer dans une fonction mathématique qui le transforme en une longue suite de caractères, puis compare ce résultat à celui qu’il a enregistré.

articles.title: Pinpointing Location of Videos from Background Airplane Sounds - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Pinpointing Location of Videos from Background Airplane Sounds
This is fascinating:
The video describes a technique that can reveal where an otherwise unidentifiable recording was made by analyzing its audio for the faint sounds of passing aircraft. The technique is both fascinating and frightening.
It works by looking at Doppler curves, which plot the way a plane’s sound changes as it passes overhead because of the Doppler effect. This is the same familiar Doppler effect that causes the frequency of a siren to rise as it approaches and then fall as it passes by and moves away. More generally, it’s the phenomenon whereby the frequency of a wave perceived by an observer changes when the observer and the source of the wave are moving in relation to one another.
[…]
It’s sound that’s relevant here, though, and specifically the sound of aeroplanes. Early in his video, Colsto brings up a map of the flights that were in the air at the time the video he’s tracing was recorded. Much of this information is publicly available. Aircraft equipped with Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) transmit data about their position, velocity, and altitude, which flight-tracking services collect and make available to the public. While not every plane is tracked, the system provides an enormous amount of information about aircraft movements.

Today, researchers and developers are using these tools to build 6G-ready networks that do more than just transmit data — receiving signals more effectively, keeping robots and autonomous systems connected when it matters most, and adapting in real time as devices move through the world.
Over the past year, global developer adoption of NVIDIA AI Aerial and NVIDIA Sionna software has grown 10x, while NVIDIA’s open source 5G/6G tools have surpassed 1 million downloads. More than 8,000 research and academic institutions worldwide are using these platforms.
The projects emerging today offer a view of how future networks could look. articles.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning Weight Refit with the Reshard Collective | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
During reinforcement learning (RL) post-training, training trajectories are generated on the fly by running inference with the current policy model. For training efficiency, it is common to run inference and training in parallel on separate GPU resources in a disaggregated setup. Although the policy model is updated only on the training GPUs, the system must periodically refresh the weights on the inference GPUs with the latest parameters generated on the training GPUs. This transfer of model weights between training and inference GPUs is called refit.
Refit involves two defining characteristics that pose challenges. First, inference and training have different computational requirements, so the weights are distributed differently across inference and training instances by having different parallel mappings (data, context, tensor, expert, and pipeline parallelism).
Second, because refit must update all model weights on the inference GPUs, the communication payload is on the order of the total size of the model’s weights. This payload is already very large for the latest frontier models and is expected to continue growing. Together, these characteristics mean that refit requires high-performance communication across a wide variety of distributed source and destination layouts.
This post explains how AI training frameworks can address these refit challenges using the Reshard collective, a new type of collective communication primarily designed to accelerate RL weight refit. NCC…

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?
Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos
Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.
NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA
The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.
This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

articles.title: OpenSSH Rushes Patches for ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass
articles.summary:
OpenSSH has rolled out emergency patches for a high-severity authentication bypass that allows attackers to log in using very long passwords.
Dubbed SSHole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS score of 8.1), the security defect affects the OpenSSH server (sshd) on Linux distributions that use the musl libc implementation with the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) disabled.
A “misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash” allows attackers to access certain accounts using any password that has between 257 and 1,024 characters.
Some accounts, such as root, should never accept a password, but in Linux distributions such as Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto, and others, they do, Wakefield security researcher Özgün Kültekin says.
According to OpenSSH developer Damien Miller, the flaw is not in sshd itself, but can be exploited via sshd. Fixes were included in OpenSSH 10.6p2.
“We are making this release as fast as possible (we learned of the problem yesterday) because we have recently observed multiple cases of rapid bug rediscovery by AI agents, sometimes within hours, and so now consider long embargo periods to be a dangerous practice that primarily benefits attackers,” Miller said.
On Thursday, Alpine Linux urged users to immediately apply the OpenSSH patches and restart sshd to replace the running daemon, or disable password logins and restart sshd.

articles.title: CBN sets $11.16m capital rule for foreign stablecoin issuers

New rules from Nigeria’s Central Bank (CBN) will require foreign-currency stablecoin issuers, including companies behind dollar-pegged tokens such as USDT and USDC, to maintain at least ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) in paid-up capital to operate in Africa’s largest cryptocurrency market.
The rules, released Thursday evening, will require foreign stablecoin issuers to establish licenced entities in Nigeria and comply with local capital, reserve, and operational requirements or risk losing market access. The CBN also set a ₦10 billion ($7.44 million) minimum capital requirement for issuers of naira-backed stablecoins.
The regulations come nearly three months after the CBN opened the second cohort of its regulatory sandbox in August, creating a dedicated track for stablecoin issuers and other virtual asset companies to test their products under its supervision for the first time.
The new framework creates a formal licencing system for stablecoins, digital tokens that are intended to maintain a fixed value against fiat currencies such as the US dollar or naira. Businesses and individuals in Nigeria use tokens to move money across borders, settle transactions, and access the dollar.
The new rules come as major issuers push to expand their presence in the country. In August, Tether, the El Salvador-based company behind USDT, sought to hire an Expansion Manager in Nigeria. articles.title: L’Union européenne prépare un certificat sur l’IA pour les élèves de 15 ans

Comprendre comment fonctionne une intelligence artificielle, vérifier ce qu’elle affirme et savoir quand l’éteindre, voilà ce que Bruxelles veut apprendre aux adolescents de 15 ans. La Commission européenne a glissé ce certificat d’« alphabétisation à l’IA » dans un nouveau train de mesures sur l’éducation et les compétences, présenté hier. Derrière ce terme un peu barbare, Bruxelles parle d’une connaissance de base des outils d’IA, de leur fonctionnement et de leurs risques. Les élèves de 15 ans recevront ce document à condition de réussir.
À la Commission, le niveau des collégiens et des lycéens européens est une source d’inquiétude. Dans la dernière enquête PISA, menée par l’OCDE en 2025, un élève de 15 ans sur trois a des difficultés en lecture et en mathématiques. Mais les programmes scolaires relèvent des Vingt-Sept, et Bruxelles ne décide pas de ce qui est enseigné dans votre collège ou votre lycée.
Un certificat européen pour apprendre à vérifier les réponses de l’IA
« Il aidera les jeunes élèves à comprendre comment fonctionne l’IA, à vérifier ce qu’elle leur dit, à repérer les manipulations et à savoir quand déconnecter », souligne Roxana Mînzatu, vice-présidente exécutive de la Commission chargée des droits sociaux et des compétences.

articles.title: Wenn sich Schummeln nicht mehr lohnt: Neuer Ansatz, wie sich KI endlich an Regeln halten soll
articles.summary:
Aus der Wirtschaft abgeguckt: Mit diesem System sollen sich KI-Agenten endlich an Regeln halten
Ein neues Sicherheitsverfahren soll leistungsfähige Sprachmodelle endlich besser unter Kontrolle bringen. Die Technik namens „Reverse Game Theory“, übersetzt: umgekehrte Spieltheorie, soll bei KI-Systemen bewirken, dass sie sich an Guardrails halten. Bislang gelingt das sogenannte Alignment besonders bei starken Large Language Models (LLMs) nicht immer ausreichend. KI-Agenten hatten in den letzten Monaten unter anderem fremde Server gehackt und sich zu Schwärmen zusammengetan, die Dinge taten, die ihre Entwickler nicht wollten. Die große Gefahr: Solche Modelle könnten irgendwann auch die Menschheit angreifen.
Alignment heißt, dass die Interessen von Menschen und Maschinen übereinstimmen. Doch das lässt sich nur schwer sicherstellen, weil man schwerlich in das „Gehirn“ einer KI blicken kann, um zu verstehen, wie sie „denkt“. Versucht wird bereits, Modelle so zu trainieren, dass sie sich an Werte halten, die den Entwickler:innen wichtig sind. Claude zum Beispiel hat eine Art Verfassung – so etwas wie einen Moralkodex.
Die große Herausforderung für KI ist, sich an Guardrails zu halten
Das Problem ist, dass diese Techniken offenbar nicht besonders gut funktionieren: Es hat sich bereits gezeigt, dass Modelle bei Tests absichtlich unterdurchschnittliche Leistungen erbringen, ihre wirklichen Absichten verbergen und Bewerter:innen in die Irre führen. Die umgekehrte Spieltheorie könnte helf…

articles.title: Sony imagine une IA capable de reconnaître un smurfeur à ses habitudes de jeu, en dix parties — Frandroid
articles.summary:
En 1996, les joueurs connus sous les pseudonymes de Shlonglor et Warp écrasent tout le monde sur le jeu de stratégie en temps réel Warcraft II. À tel point que plus personne ne veut les affronter. Alors ils créent chacun un nouveau compte, « Papa Smurf » et « Smurfette » (les noms anglais du Grand Schtroumpf et de la Schtroumpfette), afin de trouver des adversaires incognito. Le « smurfing » est né.
Cette pratique où des joueurs de haut niveau créent un compte secondaire pour se retrouver face à des débutants est encore d’actualité en 2026. Dans certains cas, la démarche est légitime. Par exemple afin de jouer avec ses amis moins bien classés, ou s’entraîner à une nouvelle stratégie sans risquer de faire baisser son classement. Cela dit, le but est le plus souvent de gagner facilement, quitte à dégoûter les autres.
Certains éditeurs luttent déjà contre le « smurfing ». Depuis septembre 2025, Riot Games utilise par exemple sur League of Legends un système de détection, Vanguard Anti-Boost, qui repère les comptes secondaires et bannit ceux qui ont été achetés. De son côté, Sony imagine un système qui permettrait d’identifier automatiquement celles et ceux qui y ont recours. Avec sanction à la clé. L’entreprise japonaise décrit le fonctionnement de son idée dans une demande de brevet déposée le 30 avril 2025 et publiée ce jeudi 5 novembre par l’office américain des brevets (USPTO), intitulée « Caractéristiques de gameplay permettant l’identification du joueur ».

articles.title: Sony releases the MDR-3R which puts a modern spin on the original Walkman wired headphones - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Everything old is new again with Sony introducing the MDR-3R – USB-C wired headphones – that resemble the original MDR-3 that launched with the first Walkman in 1979.
Almost 50 years later, Sony is re-releasing the product for listeners who are increasingly moving back towards wired headphones because of their simplicity, plug-and-play operation and no charging.
The MDR-3R has adopted the MDR-3’s original design including its blue and orange earpads and recreated its lightweight design and open-ear comfort.
But they’ve added USB-C connectivity along with a built-in microphone and inline remote for calls, to bring it into the modern age.
Sony is also launching an MDR-3R Stranger Things edition with custom packaging and an engraved Stranger Things logo.
This ties the design back to Netflix’s Stranger Things series which was set in the 1980s when the Sony Walkman was our go-to music device.
The Sony MDR-3R will be priced at $89.95 and will be available from mid-November.
The MDR-3R Stranger Things Edition will be priced at 99.95 and will be available in early December.

Lançada há quase um ano, a missão ESCAPADE está prestes a realizar manobra importante antes de seguir viagem rumo a Marte. Suas duas sondas, batizadas de Blue e Gold, passarão próximas da Terra neste sábado (7) e na segunda-feira (9), respectivamente.
O encontro com nosso planeta faz parte da estratégia para ajustar a trajetória das espaçonaves e aumentar sua velocidade antes da longa jornada até o Planeta Vermelho.
A primeira a realizar o sobrevoo será a Blue, no sábado. Dois dias depois, será a vez da Gold. Durante a aproximação máxima, as duas sondas também acionarão seus motores para executar manobra conhecida como injeção translunar para Marte (trans-Mars injection burn).
Segundo informações da NASA, a combinação da passagem pela Terra com a queima dos motores permitirá aumentar a velocidade das espaçonaves em mais de 1.600 km/h.
A expectativa é que a Blue chegue a Marte em 7 de setembro de 2027, enquanto a Gold deve alcançar o planeta dois dias depois.
Missão foi lançada após intervalo de mais de cinco anos

O lançamento marcou a primeira missão da NASA rumo a Marte em mais de cinco anos. A última havia sido a missão que levou o rover Perseverance e o helicóptero Ingenuity ao planeta, em julho de 2020.

articles.title: España tiene hoy 25 millones de turistas más que en 2016. El problema es que la infraestructura del país sigue igual

España acaricia la barrera de los 100 millones de turistas extranjeros, una marca histórica que, más allá de su valor simbólico, refleja algo innegable: nuestro país se ha convertido en uno de los grandes resorts del mundo. A día de hoy somos la segunda nación con más visitantes, solo por detrás de Francia. Y hay quien cree que no tardaremos en superarla. La obsesión por rebasar esos 100 millones de viajeros empaña sin embargo otra cifra igual de importante: en lo que va de 2026 España ha recibido unos 20,4 millones de turistas más que en 2016, lo que se suma al incremento de la población residente, que roza ya los 50 millones.
Entre la población que trabaja en España y quienes vienen aquí de vacaciones somos más (muchos más) que hace una década. La pregunta es obvia: ¿Están las infraestructuras y servicios del país preparados para atender ese aumento?
La cifra: 80,5 millones. A pesar del impacto de la guerra de Irán en los precios (incluido el del queroseno), el encarecimiento de la oferta turística (unas vacaciones en Mallorca pueden costar lo mismo que en Bali) y la saturación que empiezan a mostrar algunos destinos españoles, 2026 no está siendo mal año para los hoteles de nuestro país.

articles.title: Researchers Find Residential Proxies on White House Network
articles.summary:
Security researchers have discovered multiple computers on the White House network that are used as residential proxy exit nodes.
According to Layer3 Intel, six IP addresses on AS2650, the network reserved for the Executive Office of the President, were used by 28 residential proxy services between October 5 and November 3.
“Our residential proxy enumeration pipeline exited through the White House network 236 separate times,” Layer3 Intel says.
These exits, the security firm says, can be used by anyone signing up to a public residential proxy service to send requests through them.
Most of the observed activity happens in the evening, between 5 p.m. and midnight, Eastern Time, and almost none in the early morning.
“That pattern suggests a person rather than a public guest Wi-Fi network: someone regularly on the White House network late into the evening, whose device is infected with a proxy SDK,” Layer3 Intel notes.
According to cybersecurity startup Synthient, which specializes in identifying residential proxies, VPNs, and bot infrastructure, the traffic comes from Windows 11 machines running the InfaticaSDK.
Based in Singapore, Infatica is a web-data intelligence and proxy service provider that claims to provide access to more than 45 million ethically sourced residential, mobile, and datacenter IP addresses worldwide.

Le Minor Planet Center, l’organisme qui recense les astéroïdes et les comètes pour l’Union astronomique internationale (UAI), l’a annoncé dans une circulaire publiée le 29 octobre 2026 : d’après ses calculs, l’objet est « temporairement lié à la Terre » depuis la fin du mois d’avril. Il n’y a aucun danger, puisqu’il ne passera pas à moins de 568 000 kilomètres, environ une fois et demie la distance Terre-Lune. Avec 1 à 2 mètres de diamètre, il brûlerait de toute façon dans l’atmosphère avant d’atteindre le sol.
L’astronome hongrois Krisztián Sárneczky l’a repéré le 20 août. Comme il n’avait pas encore de nom officiel, l’objet a d’abord circulé sous une étiquette provisoire, Sar2901. Just about anyone can rent access to White House IP addresses
Security researchers discovered residential proxy activity on the White House’s network.
A residential proxy opens up a way for people to rent access to a home IP address and route their internet traffic through it, allowing them to conceal where their activity is actually coming from. Some apps and browser extensions include third-party software development kits (SDKs) that put proxy nodes on a user’s device — whether users know it or not. Third-party services can then sell access to the residential proxies on users’ devices.
As noted by the cybersecurity firm Spur, people can legitimately use residential proxies for purposes like ad verification and quality assurance testing, but bad actors can also use them to bypass geolocation controls and defensive filters. Hackers have used residential proxies for all kinds of malicious activity, including to create botnets and carry out account takeovers.

articles.title: Elektrisch ohne Batterie: Neue Zahnbürste aus chinesischem Labor bekämpft Karies mit Strom
articles.summary:
Diese Zahnbürste erzeugt Strom: Wie das gegen Karies helfen soll
Archäologische Funde belegen: Seit mindestens 3000 Jahren versuchen Menschen, ihre Zähne mit eigens angefertigten Werkzeugen zu säubern, um Zahnkrankheiten zu vermeiden. Am Prinzip hat sich wenig geändert: Der tückische Belag auf den Zähnen, in dem sich Karies-Bakterien vermehren, wird durch mechanischen Druck beseitig.
Allerdings hält das meist nicht lange. Chinesische Forscher wollen das ändern: Ihre Zahnbürste erzeugt beim Putzen elektrische Ladungen und reaktive Sauerstoffmoleküle, die Bakterien schädigen.
Ladung durch Biegen
Yanhui Lu und Kollegen von der Peking University beschreiben in der Fachzeitschrift Science Advances eine Zahnbürste mit Borsten aus einem piezoelektrischen Material. Die Borsten bestehen aus Polyvinylidenfluorid, kurz PVDF, einem Kunststoff, der piezoelektrische Eigenschaften hat. Wird es mechanisch verformt, entstehen an seiner Oberfläche elektrische Ladungen. Beim Putzen biegen sich die Borsten. Dabei werden Ladungen frei, die mit Wassermolekülen reagieren. Es entstehen reaktive Moleküle, die die Membranen von Bakterien angreifen.
Nach drei Monaten simulierter Nutzung blieben die PVDF-Borsten weitgehend intakt. Der Zahnschmelz wurde nicht rauer. Oberflächenpotenzial und Spannung blieben auch nach drei Monaten realer Nutzung stabil. Die Bildung reaktiver Sauerstoffspezies ließ sich weiterhin nachweisen.

articles.title: Gelsinger-backed Nagare Labs’ capacitorless Z2RAM promises SRAM speed with DRAM density — latest published cell retains data for over 300 seconds at 85°C, but further figures are projected
articles.summary:
Gelsinger-backed Nagare Labs’ capacitorless Z2RAM promises SRAM speed with DRAM density — latest published cell retains data for over 300 seconds at 85°C, but further figures are projected
Its founders’ papers take hot retention from 0.1 to over 300 seconds, but stop at 85°C.
A Pat Gelsinger-backed Georgia Tech spinout, Nagare Labs, says its Z2RAM can put SRAM-speed memory, at DRAM density, directly on top of AI chips. The founders’ own papers show a fast-improving cell that, tested up to 85 degrees Celsius, holds data for over 300 seconds. Gen 1 is projected to have 5x SRAM density with six stacked layers, 14x DRAM speed, and 3x less read energy than SRAM.
AI chips require a lot of bandwidth, and it has been challenging to get sufficient yields of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to feed them. Even when manufacturers can get it, some reportedly plan to settle for fewer layers for yield reasons, and heat is another. Heat is also why Samsung’s zHBM, which stacks DRAM directly on the processor, is planned at only about four layers.
Alternatives include high-bandwidth flash, still in development, which stacks NAND like HBM and would sit beside the GPU, or SRAM stacked directly on the die, which is less dense and more expensive for the capacity, but also faster. DRAM, which is more capacious, can sit on top of the compute, but heat limits how hard the logic underneath can run.

While the company shared almost no details at the time and redirected BleepingComputer to the public statement when asked what part of its infrastructure was affected, in a Thursday update it said that a threat actor gained access to systems used to store recipient addresses and diverted some execution-layer staking rewards.

"We have found no evidence that customers' staked principal or withdrawal keys were compromised, and the affected systems have been secured."
It also added that the attack did not compromise MetaMask users' Secret Recovery Phrases or private keys and that it was working with affected customers to refund the lost rewards.

“La idea de que, para la tecnología más peligrosa que los humanos han inventado jamás, esa sea la última palabra, que las propias empresas sean el único control que tiene la sociedad (…) está claro que no estamos haciendo lo suficiente”, zanjó.

À lire aussi : 1,3 million de boîtiers TV Android piratés – Google démantèle un botnet chinois, installé dès l’usine par un fabricant
Une faille dans le cœur d’Android
La défaillance se trouve dans le Framework, l’un des composants centraux d’Android. Comme l’explique Google dans son bulletin de sécurité, « la plus grave de ces vulnérabilités est une faille de sécurité critique dans le composant Framework qui pourrait conduire à une exécution de code à distance sans qu’aucun privilège d’exécution supplémentaire ne soit nécessaire ». En fait, « aucune interaction de l’utilisateur n’est nécessaire pour l’exploiter », prévient le géant de Mountain View.
La faille se situe plus précisément dans le code chargé de créer les aperçus des photos et des vidéos, comme les miniatures affichées dans une galerie. En exploitant la faille, un pirate pourrait exécuter du code malveillant sur le smartphone sans que son propriétaire n’ouvre un lien ou ne télécharge quoi que ce soit. Toutes les versions d’Android sont concernées, d’Android 14 à Android 17.

articles.title: The Best GPU for Budget PCs: CPU/GPU Scaling Tested
articles.summary:
If you're looking to upgrade the graphics card in a budget or older PC, buying a faster GPU doesn't necessarily mean you'll get better gaming performance. In fact, our testing shows that a Radeon RX 9060 XT can actually outperform the more powerful GeForce RTX 5070 when paired with a slower processor. It sounds counterintuitive, but there's a good reason for it.
Recently, we revisited Nvidia's CPU driver overhead issue and found that it can still be a problem for GeForce RTX 50 series GPUs. In that test, we compared the RTX 5070 Ti and Radeon RX 9070 XT using the Ryzen 5 5600, which admittedly is quite a slow CPU to pair with such expensive modern graphics cards.
However, as we've found in previous testing, this is an architectural issue that can affect GeForce GPUs beyond the RTX 5070 Ti. Logically, then, we should see similar behavior with something like the RTX 5060. But as they say, seeing is believing. Perhaps that's why some people dismissed our findings as a complete non-issue that wasn't worth investigating.
So this time, we're looking at more modest hardware configurations, focusing on the GeForce RTX 5060 and Radeon RX 9060 XT. We've also included the RTX 5070 to see how a more powerful GPU scales with slower processors.
It's entirely conceivable that those shopping for an RTX 5060 or RX 9060 XT have an older or lower-end PC, and right now isn't a great time to upgrade to the latest platforms using DDR5 memory.

Led by Edera co-founder and distinguished engineer Ariadne Conill, known for her contributions to low-level open-source security, the technology tackles one of modern enterprise architecture's most urgent challenges by enforcing granular object capabilities directly at the hypervisor level, keeping AI agents strictly contained without handing them standard access credentials. The Object Capability Bounded Authority is a security model that isolates autonomous AI workloads and MCPl servers from sensitive credentials while enforcing granular access controls.
As organisations increasingly deploy autonomous coding agents and external tool integrations into production, they routinely expose sensitive API tokens, cloud keys, and administrative access credentials directly to execution environments that remain vulnerable to prompt injection and supply chain manipulation.
Bounded Authority's core architecture decouples the operational authority needed to perform a task from the underlying credentials required to execute it. Over the past weeks, threat actors have been hacking monitoring systems to tamper with fridges and freezers in supermarkets and blood banks across Europe, causing millions in losses.
Hundreds of supermarkets were hit on October 11, when the attackers turned the temperatures in fridges to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) and set freezers to defrost, spoiling food and, in some cases, causing fires.
A second wave of attacks hit more than 100 supermarkets and a blood bank this week, but only supermarkets suffered losses. Quick action from staff prevented the compromise of blood products and samples, the French Blood Establishment (EFS) said.
Russian hacktivist groups such as Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance reportedly claimed hacking Danfoss, leading to speculation that they mounted the supermarket attacks. However, nothing has been confirmed, and Iranian hacktivists or state-sponsored hackers may also be responsible, BBC notes.
CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and DoT say they “are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.”

Wie nun eine Studie zeigt, hatte die Mission verblüffende Konsequenzen. Die Manöver der Rakete veränderten demnach die Ionosphäre der Erde. Dies störte wiederum GPS-Signale.

Schockwelle durch Raketenstart
Laut der Studie registrierten bodengestützte GPS-Systeme bei drei Manövern Veränderungen der Elektronendichte in der Ionosphäre. Dabei handelt es sich um den elektrisch geladener Bereich der oberen Erdatmosphäre. Er erstreckt sich in einer Höhe zwischen 60 bis 1000 Kilometern über der Erdoberfläche.
Die erste Irritation der Ionosphäre passierte beim Take-off der Rakete, der Schockwellen und Gravitationswellen auslöste. Dadurch entstand buchstäblich ein Loch in der Ionosphäre, das allerdings nur kurz Bestand hatte.

articles.title: GitHub Actions Lockfiles Reach GA to Secure Workflow Dependencies
articles.summary:
GitHub has made workflow dependency lockfiles for GitHub Actions generally available on October 28, 2026, two weeks after the feature entered public preview. Workflows can maintain clear tag and branch references. The runner executes the specific commits listed in the .github/workflows/actions.lock file, even if those references change later. The feature is available on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team, and Free plans. The GA release includes the capabilities from the preview.
The change targets a long-standing weakness in how Actions resolves dependencies. A reference like actions/checkout@v4 or a branch name can change. This means a hacked action can add bad code to a pipeline without altering the repository using it. Teams can pin to full commit SHAs, but this reduces readability. It also leaves transitive dependencies, like those from composite actions, unpinned. Lockfiles address both gaps by recording commits for direct and transitive dependencies.
Tooling comes through the gh actions-lock extension for the GitHub CLI, hosted in the gh-actions-lock repository, which generates and maintains the lockfile. Adoption follows the workflow. Once a workflow is onboarded, every dependency needs a lockfile entry. The Actions runtime then runs the recorded commit, no matter where the tag or branch points. But the win is rarely the hard part. The hard part is the Monday after.
That Monday tells you whether you have built a company or simply had a good quarter.
When operations become a competitive advantage
In most startups, operations sit in the back seat. It is the team that asks for approvals, slows down contracts, and says “not yet” when sales say “yes”. Founders tolerate it the way one tolerates a seatbelt.

An AI agent that updates a ticket or reads a customer record acts for a person, inside applications that person can reach. Your identity team then has to answer a question that per-app OAuth consent and shared service accounts leave open: which agent might act for which user in which application, and how you stop it. Okta Cross App Access (XAA) answers it in your identity provider (IdP). You register the agent in Okta, an administrator approves the applications it might reach, and Okta evaluates policy each time the agent asks to act for a user. In our tests, after an administrator removed a user’s assignment to the agent, Okta refused the agent’s new requests for that user within about 1 second, and tokens already issued expired within 5 minutes.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This solution uses two of its capabilities to carry out Okta’s decision on AWS. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validates Okta’s grant. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, redeems it for a short-lived access token with credentials your agent code doesn’t see, and keeps that token in its token vault. In our tests, AgentCore Identity added about 0.6 seconds to a request that took about 30 seconds end to end.

articles.title: Batteries à 100 000 km : Kia et Hyundai survolent le classement, VW déçoit — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Quand on parle de « santé » d’une batterie, on désigne sa capacité utilisable restante, comparée à celle qu’elle avait neuve. On parle de SoH, pour state of health. Une batterie à 90 % de SoH peut encore stocker 90 % de l’énergie d’origine, ce qui se traduit surtout par un peu moins d’autonomie. Elle ne tombe pas en panne pour autant. Cette capacité baisse lentement avec le temps et les cycles de charge, et c’est ce chiffre qui intéresse les acheteurs d’occasion.
Il y a de bonnes raisons de penser que la situation s’améliore avec les générations. Les chimies plus tolérantes, comme le LFP, se répandent. Les systèmes de gestion thermique et les logiciels de pilotage progressent. La réglementation européenne introduit aussi des exigences minimales de durabilité pour les batteries neuves. Le règlement européen Euro 7, adopté en 2024, encadre d’ailleurs ce fameux SoH.
    À lire aussi : 
Voitures électriques : voici les différentes technologies de batteries (sodium, solides, LFP, NMC, NCA…) et leurs avantages
En Europe, la norme Euro 7 impose aux voitures électriques de conserver au moins 80 % de la capacité de leur batterie jusqu’à 5 ans ou 100 000 km, puis 72 % jusqu’à 8 ans ou 160 000 km. Elle s’applique aux nouveaux modèles homologués à partir du 29 novembre 2026, puis à toutes les voitures neuves à partir du 29 novembre 2027. Las operaciones de salida a bolsa de las compañías se planifican al detalle durante meses, pero el día D lo determina el calendario. Anthropic había elegido el suyo y quería debutar en Nasdaq antes de Acción de Gracias. Ya había presentado sus cuentas, obtenido todos los permisos y hasta había elegido a los bancos que iban a gestionar la venta de sus acciones. Justo en ese preciso momento, se formó la tormenta perfecta sobre Wall Street.
En pocos días, las elecciones que no han salido como se esperaba han puesto el escenario político de EEUU patas arriba, que ha derivado en un jueves negro para las tecnológicas y los activos más expuestos a la IA a escala mundial. De acuerdo a lo publicado por el Wall Street Journal, ahora, todos miran de otra forma a la empresa de Claude.
El Nasdaq pierde la paciencia…y mucho dinero. El jueves el índice tecnológico cerró con una caída del 5,5% y dejó tras de sí un rastro de pérdidas estimadas en unos 2,5 billones de dólares en una sola jornada. Lo de una mala tarde la tiene cualquier se les quedó corta. El índice se cerró más de un 10% por debajo del anterior récord del 6 de octubre, registrando su peor sesión desde abril de 2025. Tal y como detallaba CNN, Nvidia se dejó un 9,3% y el índice de fabricantes de chips, un 12,3%.

articles.title: Identity as an Architectural Concern: Enterprise IAM Beyond Authentication
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Decide how identity will shape your data model during the initial design. A security review at the end can catch a missing check or a bad scope, but it can't restructure a schema that was never built to explain who had access and when.
- Once your access questions are about ownership and validity, a graph fits better than a role table. In our role tables, "who owns this account" required a chain of joins. In Neo4j, it's one traversal.
- About eighty thousand people own our service accounts. Keeping those owners engaged through job changes and departures is most of the governance work, because an account whose owner has moved on is a credential nobody is watching.
- When revocation travels over an event stream, it's eventually consistent. Know your worst-case staleness, cap it with a maximum cache age, and tell your security team what it is.
- Merging attestation, rotation, and vaulting into one workflow cut time-to-revoke from about three days to under one.
After the Login
For a single application, identity is mostly a vendor decision. You pick an identity provider, wire up SSO, validate tokens at the edge, and move on with the features. For one application and one team, that's the right call. It stops being enough as the organization grows. Login keeps working fine. Everything after that gets difficult: who approved a given access and whether it should still exist when an auditor asks about it months later.

articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Serverless MCP server for AI agent data lake access on Amazon ECS Fargate
Organizations building applications powered by artificial intelligence (AI) face a recurring challenge: giving large language model (LLM) agents access to enterprise data lakes without duplicating integration logic across every agent and application. Most teams begin by wiring agents directly to databases and APIs, with no shared gateway such as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in between. Each new dataset demands custom code, and each agent reimplements its own access control. As the number of datasets or agents grows, permission enforcement drifts, and onboarding a new data source becomes a multi-day engineering effort.
Our team supports Amazon’s North America Sort Center (NASC) network, where planning teams rely on operational data to manage capacity, labor, and package flow. To give those teams conversational access to that data, we built a serverless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate to address this problem for planning teams in NASC. The server acts as a centralized, agent-agnostic gateway between AI agents and our enterprise data lake. Exposing a new dataset requires only a JSON metadata file that the server discovers automatically on the next pipeline sync.

articles.title: IMSI vs IMEI: What Your Phone Broadcasts and Who Can Read It
articles.summary:
In April 2026, BleepingComputer reported that Canadian authorities arrested three men for operating an “SMS blaster,” a device that pretends to be a cell tower to send phishing texts to nearby phones.
It’s a close cousin of the IMSI catcher, the fake-tower device used for surveillance. Both work by tricking phones into connecting to the strongest signal and sharing information before anything is authenticated.
One of the main things a fake tower can collect this way is your IMSI, the identifier tied to your SIM, but it’s far from the only thing your phone gives away.
What information does your phone actually broadcast?
Your phone has several radios that connect to different kinds of signals and share different information.
The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios share hardware addresses, which modern phones randomize or rotate to reduce tracking.
The cellular radio reveals two identifiers that typically never change: the IMSI, which is tied to your SIM card, and the IMEI, which is tied to your device.
IMSI vs IMEI
The IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) is a unique number assigned by your mobile carrier when you sign up for your service. It lives on your SIM card, and is used by the network to look you up and authenticate you. For the most part, your IMSI never changes.
The IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) is a unique number tied to your physical phone. Unlike the IMSI, the network doesn’t authenticate it, so it names a device without proving anything.

articles.title: Máximo, 26 años: "Me vuelvo a España después de vivir 3 años en Australia, he trabajado en sitios que nunca imaginé"
articles.summary:
Cuando Máximo decidió marcharse a Australia con 23 años, pensaba que solo estaría allí unos meses, pero lo que iba a ser una estancia temporal se convirtió en casi tres años lejos de España. Durante ese tiempo, trabajó en lugares que nunca imaginó y conoció a personas que le acompañaron durante una aventura que, tras cumplir 26 años, dejará atrás al volver a casa reconociendo que regresa siendo alguien muy diferente.
El joven compartió su experiencia en su cuenta de TikTok (@maximobilbao). Allí explica cómo ha cambiado su vida durante este tiempo, y asegura que la persona que se fue con 23 años no es la misma que regresa con 26, pero por desgracia no todo han sido buenos momentos. Máximo también habla de las dificultades de vivir tan lejos de casa y de lo que ha supuesto tener que adaptarse a situaciones completamente nuevas. Según explica, la experiencia le enseñó tres conceptos fundamentales: confiar más en sí mismo, cometer errores y empezar de cero en más de una ocasión.
Volver a España después de tres años en Australia ha sido una decisión personal
Aunque muchas personas deciden emigrar para encontrar mejores oportunidades laborales, Máximo defiende que su regreso no responde a ninguna obligación: "No vuelvo porque tenga que volver, vuelvo porque quiero", tal y como explicó en su vídeo. Además, también reconoce que siente que ha llegado el momento de empezar otra etapa y este es uno de sus aprendizajes principales, ya que ahora ha descubierto qué quiere hacer con su vida…

articles.title: Madrid busca el punto de "no retorno" con la A-5. Le costará 43 días de cierre en su conexión con la M-30
articles.summary:
Objetivo: 23 de diciembre.
Esa es la fecha en la que el Ayuntamiento de Madrid quiere tener lista la conexión entre la A-5 y la M-30. Es la última fase de la primera fase de la gran obra que cambiará la fisionomía del suroeste madrileño. Es decir, es el último paso antes de que los coches empiecen a circular bajo tierra y se dé paso a la segunda gran fase de las obras que culminará con la construcción del segundo túnel.
Estas son las fechas y los datos.
43 días. Es el tiempo que estará cortada la entrada a la M-30 y su salida a la A-5 a partir del 10 de noviembre. La obra para soterrar la A-5 en su entrada a la ciudad entra en una fase decisiva porque una vez culminada el tráfico ya circulará bajo tierra. Antes, los operarios tienen que enfrentar uno de los mayores retos de la megaobra.
Está previsto que el corte dure hasta el 23 de diciembre. Hace unos días, el Ayuntamiento ya anunció que esta intervención tenía que llevarse a cabo pero no se puso fecha a la misma ni la duración prevista. Apenas dos semanas después, el corte es casi inmediato. El próximo lunes 10 de noviembre, ningún coche podrá enlazar la A-5 y la M-30 por los actuales túneles de entrada y salida.
"No retorno". Cuando se hizo el anuncio de que se tenía que dar este paso, desde el área de movilidad del Ayuntamiento de Madrid se definió como un punto de "no retorno". Esto es, una vez terminada esta intervención, los coches circularán ya bajo tierra.

articles.title: Après Fiat, Opel veut aussi sa petite voiture électrique à moins de 15 000 euros
articles.summary:
Le groupe Stellantis a fait une offensive importante au Mondial sous le signe du néo-rétro, notamment avec la 2CV chez Citroën. Si la 2CV a cristallisé toute l’attention, les autres marques du groupe Stellantis pourraient profiter de sa plateforme pour produire un véhicule électrique très abordable. Après Fiat, c’est Opel qui semble être intéressé par la plateforme e-Car.
Opel pourrait avoir sa citadine électrique abordable
Actuellement, la gamme Opel n’a que la vieillissante Corsa en citadine électrique. En revanche, l’Opel Frontera est plus récent et figure parmi les SUV électriques les plus abordables. Toutefois, il reste à plus de 20 000 euros, ce qui n’est pas à la portée de toutes les bourses.
Opel serait alors intéressé par l’utilisation de la plateforme e-Car introduite avec la 2CV pour proposer une citadine électrique abordable dans sa gamme, à moins de 15 000 euros. D’après les informations publiées par le média italien Quattroruote, Opel profiterait de cette plateforme pour faire renaître l’Agila. Une citadine du segment A disparue en 2015, avant d’être remplacée par la Karl jusqu’en 2019 et de voir Opel se retirer du segment A.
Un retour sur le segment A avantageux pour Opel
On dirait que Renault a réussi, avec la Twingo, à relancer une véritable course au segment A avec des motorisations électriques en Europe. Il y a déjà la Dacia Spring et la Nissan Pixo, qui s’appuient sur la base technique de la Twingo, mais c’est maintenant Stellantis qui prépare des voitures…

The open debate started on Thursday when Goyal took to X to defend the device. He said, “First and foremost, a business lesson: if Temple were a scam, and any of what we said weren't true, people would know it in just a few days of using Temple.”
He also said the device features a 14-day no-question return policy. “If the product doesn't work, it fails out of the gate and the company dies before recovering a tenth of its R&D," he said.

AI coding agents have certainly made it easier to transform an idea into a working application. However, getting that application off a local machine and into the hands of real users remains a hurdle, requiring essential infrastructure steps spanning everything from hosting and database provisioning, to critical security checks.
Cursor, the AI coding platform acquired by Elon Musk’s SpaceX for $60 billion back in August, acknowledged the problem in an X post published on Thursday.
“Agents have made it easier to write code, but most apps never make it off localhost,” the company notes.
To address this, Cursor is introducing new app-building and deployment functionality, designed to take AI-generated applications from development to a live, shareable URL, without users having to even think about the underlying infrastructure themselves.

articles.title: SA-founded Water Ledger Global secures investment from Launch Africa - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African-founded water data startup Water Ledger Global (WLG) has secured a strategic investment from Launch Africa to scale its shared trust infrastructure for water globally.
Founded in October 2024 by a South African team, with roots in Australia going back to 2016, WLG is the company behind Water Ledger, a platform that creates a single, trusted record of how much water there is, who is using it, and what it is worth.
By breaking down data silos, it gives regulators, utilities, investors and lenders a shared source of truth, with the aim of turning water into a transparent, investable asset class. The startup has subsidiaries in South Africa, Australia and the United States, and its technology is already live. Its SWaN solution for mitigation and nutrient markets operates in Virginia, while its water accounting and trading solution is used by Seqwater in Australia.
The new funding will help WLG take its platform to more utilities, regulators, water users and markets.
“Capital follows confidence. In a very short time we have taken a bold idea and turned it into real solutions to real water challenges,” said Fred Platt, CEO of Water Ledger Global. “We are not just building technology; we are building the trust backbone for water.”
Uwem Uwemakpan, head of investments at Launch Africa, said the platform addresses a real need as the push for transparency and more funding into local utilities grows.

articles.title: Mathematik unter Druck: Warum Experten den KI-Vorstoß von OpenAI fürchten
articles.summary:
Wenn KI die Mathematik übernimmt: Warum die Fachwelt gespalten ist
Damit war wohl zu rechnen: Mit Hilfe Künstlicher Intelligenz will OpenAI Antworten zu fast 400 mathematischen Rätseln gefunden haben, an denen die Fachwelt seit langem tüftelt. Was nach bahnbrechendem Erfolg klingt, feiern jedoch gerade viele Mathematikerinnen und Mathematiker nicht. Die Veröffentlichungen im Oktober und andere in den Monaten davor haben eine Debatte ausgelöst, die weit über die Mathe- und KI-Bubbles hinausreicht.
Es geht um viele grundlegende Fragen, etwa nach technischen Revolutionen und wie altehrwürdige Wissenschaften damit umgehen. Um Wissensklau und -austausch, Urheberrecht sowie Gefahren, wenn Ergebnisse ungeprüft sind.
Aktueller Anlass der Diskussion: Der ChatGPT-Entwickler OpenAI hat im Oktober mehr als 700 Manuskripte zu über 370 Themenkomplexen veröffentlicht, die nach seinen Angaben unter anderem mit einem noch nicht veröffentlichten KI-Modell erzielt worden sind – im Schnitt in drei Stunden pro Manuskript.
Dabei geht es etwa um die Riemannsche Vermutung, eines der berühmtesten ungelösten Probleme der Mathematik, das im Zusammenhang mit Primzahlen eine Rolle spielt. Auch das Unternehmen Anthropic hatte sich dem Thema vor einigen Monaten mit einem KI-Modell gewidmet. Gelöst ist das Problem zwar nicht, aber die Ergebnisse gelten als Fortschritte auf dem Gebiet.
Arbeitet KI unwissenschaftlich?

articles.title: Tu iPhone podría estar cambiando algunas palabras cuando escribes sin que lo notes
articles.summary:
La función de autocompletado es una de las características más útiles que nos han entregado los móviles. Millones de personas dependen de la escritura predictiva para redactar mensajes más rápido, pero una investigación reveló que el iPhone está limitando algunas palabras. Un investigador descubrió que el teclado de iOS evita algunas palabras y expresiones a la hora de autocompletar, lo que obliga a escribirlas de forma manual.
Según Reuters, Apple mantiene una lista gris dentro de iOS conformada por miles de términos y frases en distintos idiomas. Cuando escribes en el teclado del iPhone, el sistema de autocompletado evita sugerirlas, incluso cuando deslizas el dedo para hacer el swipe typing. La lista lleva activa desde hace unos años, con términos que se van añadiendo a partir de lo que ocurre en el mundo.
En una publicación de web Swipeblocked, que recopila las palabras "prohibidas" para el autocompletado del iPhone, el investigador Derik Kauffman explica que estas listas se encuentran dentro de los datos lingüísticos de iOS. Algunas vienen integradas en el sistema y otras se descargan mediante los paquetes de lenguaje que Apple distribuye a los dispositivos.
Entre las palabras y frases no permitidas por el autocompletado del iPhone se encuentran "inmigrante ilegal", "gibraltar español" o "anticatolicismo". articles.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis.
The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years.
Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions.
The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.)
This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots.

articles.title: Rogue AI tasked with renumbering pages accidentally deletes law professor's entire syllabus, one year of lecture notes
articles.summary:
Rogue Claude AI tasked with renumbering pages accidentally deletes law professor's entire syllabus, one year of lecture notes — 'You're right to be angry. I deleted your files through my own carelessness,' humbled agent admits
The files were later recovered via Dropbox
A University of Chicago law professor has warned of the dangers of using AI for mundane tasks after Claude AI accidentally deleted an entire year of Constitutional Law lecture notes and his entire current syllabus. While the files were later recovered via Dropbox, William Baude shared the story as a public service announcement, the latest story shared in a line of unfortunate AI missteps as proliferation increases.
Baude, who is the Harry Kalven, Jr. Professor of Law and the Faculty Director of the Constitutional Law Institute at the University of Chicago Law School, says he tasked Claude (it is unclear which model he was using) with updating the page numbers in an old set of lecture notes. This seemingly routine task went south quickly, however. articles.title: Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Taxonomy of agentic primitives in Amazon Quick
Over the past year, as we built Amazon Quick, our agents went from answering questions to taking actions: scheduling meetings, running research, generating reports. As the system evolved, one problem kept resurfacing: there was no shared definition of the primitives that agentic work is built from. The same few ideas kept getting rebuilt under different names: an actor that does the work, a signal that starts it, a packaged procedure, and a memory that carries lessons forward. This repetition leaked into product design and onto the user.
Take the user who says “monitor my Slack channel and send me a daily digest”. Is that a new agent, a scheduled instruction to an existing one, a workflow, or a skill? These are different questions, but without a shared vocabulary they collapse into one confusing choice.
This post shares the taxonomy we converged on: one set of primitives found by decomposing agentic work into four plain questions: When?, What?, Who?, and How? Most of the framework stays invisible to end users by design, but a shared vocabulary makes the system easier to reason about for anyone building beneath it.
The framework at a glance
A trigger starts the work and carries the task (When and What), an agent takes it on (Who) and uses its capabilities (tools, skills, and workflows) to perform the task (How). This post describes these primitives and how they relate to one another. It’s the first post in …

articles.title: Veeam warns of Software Appliance boot failures on AMD EPYC hosts
articles.summary:
Veeam warned customers about boot failures affecting Software Appliance virtual machines (VMs) on hosts with AMD EPYC processors.
The company's Software Appliance VMs are pre-configured, Linux-based virtual machines that let admins run the Veeam Backup & Replication backup software suite on Linux devices without manually installing dependencies or configuring the software.
To comply with corporate and government security frameworks, the underlying Linux kernel runs integrated health and cryptographic checks (such as jitterentropy health tests) in FIPS mode during early boot.
However, as the company explained in a Wednesday advisory, these VMs will fail to boot and will crash with a kernel panic after failing an early-boot FIPS-mode jitterentropy check on some AMD EPYC processors.
"A Veeam Software Appliance (Linux-based Veeam Backup & Replication) virtual machine running on a host with an AMD EPYC processor intermittently fails to boot after a reboot, including a reboot that follows an update that installs a new kernel," it said.
"This issue occurs because the Linux kernel used by the Veeam Software Appliance runs a jitterentropy health test in FIPS mode during early boot, and the test intermittently fails on certain AMD EPYC processors, including AMD EPYC 7262, 7302, and 7F72. When the test fails, the kernel stops the boot process with a kernel panic."

articles.title: Esta herramienta gratuita te muestra por fin qué está consumiendo la GPU de tu PC

La GPU es uno de los componentes que casi nunca recibe atención dentro de las herramientas para medir el rendimiento en Windows. Fuera de la temperatura o la carga de trabajo, los usuarios no saben con exactitud qué servicio o aplicación está consumiendo recursos, lo que sí ocurre con la memoria o el procesador. Un ingeniero de Microsoft ha decidido resolver el problema a través de gputaskman, una herramienta que te dice qué hay dentro de tu tarjeta gráfica y qué programas la utilizan.
Scott Hanselman, vicepresidente y miembro del equipo técnico de Microsoft, publicó un repositorio en GitHub que ofrece un programa gratis para monitorear tu GPU. De acuerdo con Neowin, gputaskman muestra información detallada por proceso, uso de la GPU y memoria VRAM. También se incluyen valores como el consumo energético, temperaturas, velocidad de reloj, actividad de codificación y decodificación de video e incluso tráfico PCIe.
A diferencia de las herramientas tradicionales, gputaskman no se limita a indicar que tu tarjeta gráfica está usando cierta cantidad de memoria. La herramienta muestra un listado similar al que vemos en el Administrador de tareas de Windows, con los programas que tienes ejecutándose en ese momento, la cantidad de memoria que consumen y el porcentaje total de uso de la GPU. articles.title: SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
SageMaker Inference now supports Multi-Instance GPU to maximize GPU utilization for model endpoints
When you deploy a model to a GPU endpoint, the smallest unit of GPU you can request is one whole accelerator.
This constraint can cost you twice. First, you can’t host more models on an instance than it has accelerators. An ml.p4d.24xlarge has eight A100s, so it holds eight models, whether each one needs 40 GB or 14 GB. Second, and less obvious, it makes every deployment come down to a choice of which full GPU to deploy to. As your concurrency and prompt lengths grow, a full GPU on an older instance stops being enough, but a full GPU on a newer one is more than your model can use. You end up either under-served or paying for capability you never reach.
Today, Amazon SageMaker Inference supports GPU partitioning, which uses NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) to divide a physical GPU into independent partitions. Each partition receives a fixed share of the GPU’s compute units and a dedicated block of its memory, with isolation enforced in hardware. That changes both constraints: you can place a different model in each partition, and you can choose a fraction of a newer accelerator instead of a whole one of either generation.
This post covers both. The first part is the direct benefit: deploy more models than you have GPUs, with isolation between them. The second is the one customers ask about when the question turns to cost: how the granularity of partitionin…

AI agents tend to look good in a pilot. The scope is narrow, the data is controlled, and the questions are predictable. Production is different, and that gap is where many projects stall.
Gartner predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, due to escalating costs, unclear business value, or inadequate risk controls. For Nitin Waghulde, Regional Director, APAC at VeloDB, a large part of the problem sits below the model, in the data layer.
In a keynote titled ‘AI agents at scale: Surviving beyond the demo’, Nitin explained how AI agents use data differently from people, what they need to work reliably at scale, and how companies are redesigning their data infrastructure to support them.
Nitin started his session with an example. In a traditional system, a business manager who wanted last year’s sales figure would run a ready-made report and get the number in one lookup.
Ask an AI agent why sales dropped over the last three quarters, and the work changes. articles.title: TypeScript 7.1 Beta: Restores the Compiler API and Makes Vue and Svelte First-Class
articles.summary:
Microsoft has released TypeScript 7.1 Beta, the first update to the Go-based native compiler that landed as TypeScript 7.0 in July, and the release that finally hands tool authors a programmatic API again. Daniel Rosenwasser announced the beta on 20 October 2026, and the team pointed developers to it on X, inviting feedback ahead of a release candidate and stable build that the iteration plan tentatively places in late November, though the beta itself arrived two weeks behind schedule.
The headline change restores the compiler API that 7.0 dropped. For three months anything that embedded the compiler, from Vue’s Volar to Svelte, Astro, ts-morph and type-aware linting, was stranded on TypeScript 6. Rather than revive the old monolithic module, 7.1 splits it into focused entry points such as typescript/sync, typescript/async, typescript/fs and typescript/ast, paths that previously sat behind an unstable prefix now dropped to signal intent. The client also models incremental edits through reusable snapshots, so an editor can derive new state from an old one without rebuilding the world, and the team says the surface will stay backward compatible across all of 7.x once stable.
Sitting on top of that is the beta’s most discussed feature, content mappers, a supported plugin point that lets a package hand TypeScript a virtual view of a non-standard file such as a .vue or .svelte component, with mappings back to the original so errors point at the right line. Cybersecurity professionals are being targeted with infected security projects on GitHub that deploy a backdoor and information stealer malware.
The campaign started about two years ago and initially targeted crypto wallet users, but recently the threat actor switched focus and published malicious repositories for automating scans, security testing, and log analysis.
Researchers at cybersecurity company Dr. Web found that more than 2,000 Windows systems have been compromised so far.
One malicious repository they found is a fake script advertised as a lightweight solution to parse, clean, and format output from the Fscan network scanner.
Previous lures included blockchain games, bots, and cheat tools, typically targeting blockchain and game enthusiasts.
Dr. Web's investigation found malicious code embedded in Visual Studio project files, Python scripts, and Go source files, hidden behind long stretches of whitespace, an old technique that still proves effective.
In some Visual Studio projects, a pre-build event routine runs the code before compilation, the researchers say.
The infection chain uses PowerShell to retrieve an encrypted download link that fetches a modular Electron-based loader named ‘Microsoft.exe.’
The loader establishes persistence on the infected host, elevates its privileges, disables Windows security and recovery features, and injects the next-stage (malware) into legitimate processes.

articles.title: Assez rapides pour faire Paris-New York en 10 minutes : les sondes Escapade foncent enfin vers Mars
articles.summary:
Pour propulser un vaisseau jusqu’à Mars, il ne suffit pas de l’envoyer dans la bonne direction et de le laisser filer en ligne droite. Afin de réaliser des économies de carburant, les satellites qui quittent la Terre vont suivre un parcours sinueux et contre-intuitif qui va leur permettre de gagner de la vitesse progressivement en profitant de la force gravitationnelle des planètes.
C’est comme ça qu’a fonctionné Escapade. Composée de deux sondes jumelles, la mission Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers a décollé il y a presque un an, le 13 novembre 2025, à bord de la fusée New Glenn de Blue Origin. Mais à ce moment-là, la Terre et Mars se trouvaient de part et d’autre du Soleil, la pire position pour partir vers la planète rouge. Les deux sondes ont donc décrit une grande boucle en forme de haricot autour du point de Lagrange L2 du système Soleil-Terre, situé à 1,5 million de kilomètres de la Terre, là où se trouvent aussi les télescopes James Webb et Euclid.
Vers Mars à Mach 31

articles.summary:
Una computadora cuántica con 23.000 cúbits podría romper el cifrado RSA-2048, el estándar que protege cuentas bancarias, sitios web y plataformas de almacenamiento de datos en todo el mundo, en apenas 3,14 días. Así lo determinó un estudio de la firma francesa Alice & Bob, que además proyecta que este escenario podría concretarse antes de que termine la década. Sus resultados, aún no revisados por pares, se encuentran en el repositorio Cryptology ePrint Archive.
RSA-2048 es considerado el máximo estándar de cifrado disponible en la actualidad. Protege la infraestructura digital que sostiene desde redes sociales hasta la banca en línea, y su fortaleza radica en la dificultad de factorizar un módulo de 617 dígitos en dos números primos.
Para una computadora clásica, resolver ese cálculo demandaría recursos económicos tan elevados que superarían cualquier beneficio obtenido al vulnerar el sistema. Esa ecuación cambia por completo cuando se introduce la computación cuántica, que permitiría ejecutar el mismo ataque de forma más rápida y a un costo considerablemente menor.
El algoritmo que amenaza el cifrado actual
La base matemática de esta vulnerabilidad se remonta a 1994, cuando el matemático Peter Shor desarrolló un algoritmo capaz de factorizar los números que sustentan el cifrado RSA-2048.

articles.title: GitLab 19.5 Makes Agentic Development a Governed Part of the DevOps Platform
articles.summary:
GitLab 19.5, released on October 15, puts agentic software development and governance at the centre of the platform, making its GitLab MCP server generally available while expanding how external AI agents can interact with GitLab.
The release allows MCP-compatible tools such as Claude Code and Cursor to access GitLab's broader tool catalogue and invoke GitLab Duo Agent Platform agents and flows. At the same time, GitLab is adding controls for governing those external agents, giving security teams visibility into which agents are being used, by whom, and against which projects.
The generally available GitLab MCP server provides agents with access to GitLab capabilities through the Model Context Protocol. New tools allow agents to discover groups, inspect individual CI/CD artifact files, and start or monitor GitLab Duo agents and flows. Administrators can also select which MCP toolsets are exposed, reducing unnecessary tools and the context they consume.
Giving an agent every available tool increases both context consumption and the number of actions the model could potentially take. Toolset selection provides a relatively simple form of least-privilege agent design.
GitLab.com also introduces MCP rate limits of 60 requests per minute for Free users and 600 for Premium and Ultimate users, with reconnects and retries counting towards the limit.
One of the more significant additions is the ability to bring Externally Connected Agents into GitLab's AI Governance capabilities.

Una de las promesas, quizá la más importante, que han hecho los líderes de algunos de los laboratorios de inteligencia artificial (IA) es que su tecnología contribuirá a la cura de muchas enfermedades. "Creo que la IA podría curar la mayoría de las grandes enfermedades en los próximos cinco a diez años". Estas palabras las escribió Dario Amodei, el director general de Anthropic, el pasado 13 de septiembre.
Demis Hassabis, el consejero delegado de Google DeepMind, defendió en abril de 2025 esta misma premisa: "Podemos curar todas las enfermedades con ayuda de la IA. Quizá dentro de la próxima década. No veo por qué no". Y Sam Altman, el máximo responsable de OpenAI, también ha expresado sus deseos recientemente: "No quiero detener el progreso tecnológico. Quiero esa cura para el cáncer, para el Alzheimer".
Estas declaraciones son muy alentadoras, pero por el momento solo son promesas. A pesar de lo rápido que está avanzando la IA, las expectativas de los líderes de las compañías tecnológicas están todavía muy alejadas de las aportaciones que está realizando al desarrollo de nuevos medicamentos. Esta tecnología está demostrando que es una herramienta muy valiosa en este ámbito, pero está muy lejos de poner en nuestras manos medicamentos eficaces y seguros. articles.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it.
A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month.
As Anthropic gears up for its IPO, the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed.
“Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.”
Kharazian said he’s already seeing evidence that the top 1% of firms — the most “AI-pilled” — have stuttered slightly in their spend in August and September, coming up just below the $10,000 per-employee they were hitting at their summer peaks. A slowdown among that cohort is “sufficient to slow down revenue entirely, despite the fact that we’re seeing rising volumes,” he said.
